items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: Number one my second group — my first group that I performed with in New York City was with Jackie McLean. He trained Bobby Hutcherson, Charles Tolliver, and let me see, and myself.

ctx.x: Well as you said, your older guys who have been around, when you moved to New York in 1964, I think I’m correct about that, I’m going to guess that as a jazz musician you had to do a certain amount of scrambling, reaching out to other people, finding a mentor, and making connections. Isn’t that part of finding out who you are, forming your personality. And I wonder if young people don’t have that opportunity now?

Young people don’t have a lot of that kind of opportunity, but as far as I’m concerned, when I arrived in New York City I needed not a sound. I had no need for a mentor. I had no need to discover myself. I had, although having not researched who was doing what at what level, etcetera, etcetera. I had studied. I wanted to be a music teacher. So I finished college before arriving in New York and I tell everybody that in college I flunked everything but I was a great student in the music area. And so when I arrived…

instrument, I mean I was in the Army before I finished college, in the band, as a clarinetist. And when the band practices were finished, for two years, I would practice my bass throughout the waning, the late hours of the evening, on and on. You know I had this inspiration to develop my personal reality. So doing that for two years, then returning to college, finishing, graduating with a degree in music education, when I arrived in New York City I felt I had something on my shoulder. items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: Jackie McLean, we did that when things were more or less in line structurally

ctx.x: Jackie McLean, we did that when things were more or less in line structurally, etcetera, etcetera. You know you would open up. That’s when they had those tapes, you know those big thick tapes. But with Pharoah I don’t recall ever doing that with anything, the things were like from A all the way to Z and past, with fury, either be it in the quietest of the night or the loudest of the center of the city.
Did you ever read reviews on some of these recordings or live gigs with Pharoah where the reviewer called the music “angry?”
